motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, Bailes and McLaughlin reported a single millisecond-duration, highly dispersed radio burst in archival Parkes pulsar data, with a dispersion measure far above the Milky Way contribution. The result met early scepticism. Their careful analysis showed the source lay at cosmological distance, and it opened a new class of astrophysical transients. Thousands of fast radio bursts have since been found, including repeaters, host galaxies and a burst from a Galactic magnetar. FRBs have become precision probes of fundamental physics. Their dispersion measures located the long-missing baryons in the intergalactic medium. They now constrain the Hubble constant, the photon mass, the equivalence principle and compact dark matter, and they map magnetised plasma across the cosmos. This discovery changed how we use radio telescopes such as CHIME, ASKAP, MeerKAT and the coming SKA to test cosmology and gravity.
